extracted.intended_audience: general readers, fans, and students/practitioners of comedy
extracted.subtask_description: Identifying and assessing features of a stand-up/comedic performance style (delivery, recurring bits, topicality, technique) using Norm Macdonald's career and comments as examples. Useful for critics, comedians, and scholars analyzing comedic voice and choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadpan delivery; eccentric understatement; folksy, old-fashioned turns of phrase
rubrics_metrics.description: Norm Macdonald's style was characterized by deadpan delivery, eccentric understatement, and the use of folksy, old-fashioned turns of phrase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This criterion emphasizes tone and diction: a flat affect (deadpan) combined with deliberately quaint or old-fashioned wording can form a distinctive comedic voice. Example: introductions or punchlines delivered without visible emotion so the content's absurdity carries the laugh. No explicit scoring guidance provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chaotic yet understated comedic style / setting expectations then 'pulling the rug out'
rubrics_metrics.description: He developed a reputation for his 'chaotic yet understated comedic style' and for comedy that 'sets your expectations before pulling the rug out from under you.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique involves shaping audience expectations (setup) and subverting them unexpectedly; the surface may seem loose or chaotic while the underlying structure is controlled. Example references: late-night appearances and interviews. Anti-pattern: jokes that appear chaotic but lack the subversive payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimalist delivery / 'no opinions' approach
rubrics_metrics.description: From May 2017 Macdonald moved to a more reserved, deadpan style, claiming to have 'no opinions' and reducing gesture and verbiage down to an absurd minimum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion focuses on economy of language and physical restraint — fewer gestures, fewer words, implying rather than stating. Guidance: minimalism can intensify absurdity; scoring would reward concision and impact. Anti-pattern: minimalism that becomes indistinguishable from flatness or disengagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of running jokes and non-sequitur punchlines
rubrics_metrics.description: He often used running jokes and non-sequitur punchlines (for example, repeatedly referencing Frank Stallone as an absurd scapegoat).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recurring bits create familiarity and build comedic payoff over time; non-sequiturs can generate surprise. Example: Frank Stallone as a repeated, absurd blame-punchline. Anti-pattern: overuse of a running gag until it loses comic value or becomes mean-spirited without payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impressions and imitation as a comic technique
rubrics_metrics.description: He performed impressions of public figures and noted that imitation was the highest form of flattery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impressions can showcase range and pay homage; effective impressions balance recognizable mimicry with comedic reinterpretation. Guidance implicit in biography: use impressions thoughtfully to serve a larger bit. Anti-pattern: impressions used as mere impersonation without comedic insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre/format choices: observational, deadpan, non-sequitur, black comedy, insult comedy, shaggy dog story, political satire
rubrics_metrics.description: Listed genres associated with Macdonald include observational comedy, deadpan, non-sequitur, black comedy, insult comedy, shaggy dog story, and political satire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selecting genre(s) informs material, pacing, and audience expectations. Guidance: align material and delivery to chosen genres; e.g., shaggy dog stories reward long setups and payoff. Anti-pattern: mixing incompatible genres without clear intent, which can confuse audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding 'low-hanging fruit' topical jokes
rubrics_metrics.description: Macdonald expressed distaste for the 'low-hanging fruit' of easy topical jokes (specifically cited Donald Trump jokes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion favors originality and depth over obvious topical jabs. Guidance: prefer material that reframes or deepens a topic rather than repeating predictable targets. Anti-pattern: relying on obvious, widely-circulated punchlines that elicit only reflexive responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be informed when attacking complex subjects (e.g., religion)
rubrics_metrics.description: While judging on Last Comic Standing, Macdonald criticized a contestant for a joke about the Harry Potter books and the Bible: 'If you're going to take on an entire religion, you should at least know what you're talking about.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule of thumb: satire or critique of religion (or other complex institutions) should be informed and specific; ignorance undermines the joke. Anti-pattern: lazy or uninformed attacks that invite backlash and weaken comedic credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Edgy or shock humor risks backlash and professional consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Some of Macdonald's jokes (e.g., about prison rape, transgender murder victim Brandon Teena, Michael Jackson, and repeated O. J. Simpson jokes) provoked sharp criticism, pickets, and, according to accounts, contributed to his removal as Weekend Update anchor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This criterion cautions that controversial material can produce significant public and institutional pushback; comedians and producers should weigh creative choices against potential consequences. Examples: NBC's review and criticism after certain Weekend Update lines; Don Ohlmeyer allegedly removed Macdonald amid conflict over Simpson jokes. Anti-pattern: assuming shock equals successful comedy without considering context or fallout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of small devices and staging (e.g., 'note to self' tape-recorder bit)
rubrics_metrics.description: He occasionally delivered a piece of news before taking out a personal compact tape recorder and leaving a 'note to self' relevant to what he just discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small theatrical devices or recurring props can add texture and a signature to a set; effective when integrated into rhythm and persona. Anti-pattern: gimmicks that distract from material or aren't tied to a comedian's voice.
